inputs.userGoal: no no data everthing is new so do whatever it takes
subGoals: Replace personal Azure resource names with professional production names without deleting existing resources before validation.
Cost-optimized: retain the existing Central India, Burstable PostgreSQL baseline and avoid premium networking until the application is operational.
Security-first: managed identity, Key Vault RBAC, HTTPS-only, WebSockets for deployment streams, and no plaintext credentials outside Key Vault.

reasoning.whyChosen: Replaces the personal-named empty vault with a globally unique professional name while retaining managed-identity access and RBAC authorization.
alternativesConsidered: Use private endpoints and disable public network access
reasoning.tradeoffs: Private endpoints require VNet integration and DNS resources that do not exist in the current cost-optimized deployment. Purge protection is deliberately irreversible once enabled.

resources.name: zeroops-prod-pg-cin-7z26
resources.subtype: Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server

reasoning.whyChosen: Creates an empty professional-named replacement matching the existing low-cost PostgreSQL capacity and version; no data migration is required.
alternativesConsidered: General Purpose zone-redundant PostgreSQL with private access
reasoning.tradeoffs: Burstable PostgreSQL, public networking, seven-day local backup, and no high availability minimize cost but are not suitable for high-availability workloads.

resources.dependencyReasoning: The generated database administrator password and the application connection string are stored only in the replacement Key Vault.

references.title: PostgreSQL Flexible Server naming and creation

resources.name: zeroops-backend-key-vault-access
resources.subtype: Key Vault Secrets Officer RBAC assignment

reasoning.whyChosen: Grants the existing zeroops-backend-id-96a7 managed identity the data-plane permissions needed to load control-plane configuration and manage project secrets.
reasoning.tradeoffs: The role can manage secrets, which is required by the existing project-secret workflow; a read-only role would break customer-secret management.

reasoning.whyChosen: Hardens the existing backend and points it to the professional Key Vault only after all required real secrets have been added.
alternativesConsidered: Deploy a new backend App Service
reasoning.tradeoffs: Always On may increase App Service cost. Reusing the existing backend avoids a new public hostname and keeps the change reversible until the old vault is removed.

overallReasoning.summary: The existing personal-named Key Vault and PostgreSQL server are empty/new and cannot be renamed. This staged plan creates professionally named replacements, preserves the existing App Services and backend managed identity, and delays cutover until configuration is complete.
overallReasoning.tradeoffs: No VNet, private endpoints, Application Insights, Log Analytics, zone-redundant database, or geo-redundant backup are added because the current Azure for Students deployment is cost-optimized. These omissions must be addressed before a high-availability production launch. SMTP credentials are unknown and will not be fabricated; backend cutover remains blocked until they are supplied.

plan.validation: All replacement names satisfy documented Azure naming constraints; Key Vault name availability was confirmed. PostgreSQL global availability will be checked at create time with a safe alternate suffix if needed. No current data requires migration.
architecturePrinciples: Secret values stored only in Key Vault
Preserve current resources until replacement validation
